jobs.description:
Job Description

Fugro USA Land, Inc., seeks Senior Geologist. Worksite 201 N Civic Drive #360, Walnut Creek, CA 94596 (Partial telecommuting – 2 days per week). Offered salary $123,240 per year. (REQ # R0031542
) on resume.

Duties And Responsibilities

Under the direction of the Principal Geologist, demonstrate proficient report/proposal writing and verbal communication skills. Work on geologic hazard assessment and site characterization for various infrastructure projects, especially fault studies, seismic hazard assessments, seismic source modeling and catalog development, field mapping, geologic interpretation of geotechnical and geospatial data, and geologic hazard assessments. Conduct fieldwork including rock, soil sampling, geologic mapping and site assessment; assist in analyzing geologic data, interpreting findings and prepare reports; support drilling operations including core logging and sample preparation; utilize geologic software to interpret and present data; ensure compliance with environmental and safety regulations; collaborate with other geologists and engineers to support project developments; maintain accurate records of geologic and geotechnical observations, test results, and site conditions, assist in laboratory testing and analysis; work on desktop studies; and support proposal preparation. Mentor junior staff. Work on business/client development, with lead role on proposal presentation. Manage all aspects of multiple small to mid-size projects/year (budget, schedule, scope of work, client relations). Support technical needs of clients. Involvement and participation in the design, implementation, and supervision of field exploration programs, and detailed site characterization studies. Participate in the development of the scope, estimating costs, and procuring subcontractors. Develop and adhere to reasonable project schedules and deadlines. Research and data analysis. Perform engineering geologic analyses and develop reasonable conclusions and recommendations. Develop seismic source models and earthquake catalogs. Prepare technical reports in a timely, organized, and accurate manner. Develop positive client relationships. Maintain positive reputation in professional community. Contribute to positive corporate reputation. Help develop project opportunities. Participate in and support continuous improvement of the company's processes, including safety and quality. Perform other duties as may be assigned.

Required Education And Experience

Master's degree in Engineering Geology, or Geological Engineering.
2 years of field experience in soil and rock logging, geologic mapping, site characterization, and paleoseismological trenching for fault investigations; experience with geologic and geotechnical data interpretation, integration of downhole geophysical data, and development of geologic models to support engineering decisions; experience preparing technical reports and desktop studies, managing projects—including those in the nuclear power projects—and performing rock mass characterization; synthesize complex geological data to assess site conditions and support multidisciplinary project teams.
Special Requirement
Any understanding of geohazards and their implications for project planning and development.
Partial telecommuting – 2 days per week
25% of domestic travel.

jobs.description:
Tactica Solutions is seeking an experienced Geospatial Analyst Expert to support the U.S. Army INSCOM APOGEE program at Fort Gordon. This is a high-impact opportunity to apply advanced geospatial analysis and GIS expertise in direct support of critical Army and national intelligence requirements.

In this role, you will bring deep knowledge of the full spectrum of government and commercial GEOINT capabilities, spatial data processing, analytic modeling, and industry-standard tools such as Esri ArcGIS, QGIS, MapBox, and GeoServer to solve complex geospatial intelligence challenges. You will work side-by-side with partners across the Intelligence Community and Department of Defense, producing clear, actionable geospatial intelligence through well-crafted reports, graphics, briefings, and multimedia presentations that senior leaders rely on.

At Tactica, we value sharp analysts who take ownership of their work and contribute to a collaborative, mission-focused team. If you are ready to put your geospatial expertise to work on a program that matters, we want to talk with you.

Why this role stands out

Direct support to INSCOM’s GEOINT mission
Onsite work at Fort Gordon with a dedicated team
Opportunity to apply advanced GIS, spatial modeling, and geospatial data expertise to real operational decisions

Responsibilities

The Geospatial Analyst shall perform analysis of the full spectrum of US Government and commercial GEOINT assets and maintain expertise in all associated tradecraft, including Synthetic Aperture RADAR (SAR), Electro-Optical (EO), Moving Target Indicator (MTI), Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR), Overhead Persistent Infrared (OPIR), Geospatial Information and Services (GI&S), Wide Area Persistent Surveillance (WAPS), geospatial data processing, analysis and modeling, and general intelligence analysis.
Maintain proficiency with all tools and databases necessary to access supporting intelligence information required for the execution of GEOINT support to the customer.
Use geographic information systems, methods, and tools to answer critical intelligence questions.
Perform specialized scientific and technical data processing techniques utilizing non-standard and developmental software suites, to include SAP, CAP, and CNWDI level programs; stage for exploitation; and provide requisite training as required by the Government.
Adhere to all GEOINT related technical publications, policies, and directives at the National, Theater, and local level.
Responsible for capturing analytical findings in textual, graphic, vector, or other formats as directed by national land local policy and will ensure that GEOINT reporting adheres to national, theater, and local policies which govern content, accuracy, formatting, classification, and timeliness.
Maintain familiarity and expertise with all relevant classification guides, security policy, and Intelligence Community Directives (ICDs).
Remain abreast of geo-political events, topics, atmospherics, and current events as they relate to supported Combatant Commands and respective theaters, to provide informed, insightful, and timely answers to customer intelligence requirements.
dditional duties as assigned or required.

Education & Experience

MA or MS in a technical field such as Geomatics, Geospatial Sciences, or related degree AND 10 years of relevant experience; OR BA/BS degree in a technical field such as Geomatics, Geospatial Sciences, or related degree AND 15 years of relevant experience
College degree must be in Geospatial Information & Services (GIS), Geomatics, Geospatial Sciences, or related field.

Clearance

Current/active TS/SCI security clearance with Single Scope Background Investigation (SSBI).

Technical Skills & Knowledge

Relevant experience must be in geospatial analysis and/or geospatial information systems.
Expert knowledge of industry standard location analysis desktop and server applications such as Esri ArcGIS Platform, QGIS, MapBox, GeoServer, etc.
Experience using and managing spatial relational databases including Oracle, MSSQL, or PostGreSQL/PostGIS.
Extensive experience with geographically-derived assessments, enterprise data integration, spatial data governance, metadata management and interpretation of business and performance metrics.
Demonstrated experience using geospatial Python, R, SAS, Java or other coding languages to deliver custom geoprocessing and analytical workflows.

Core Competencies

Expert ability to present geospatial information via multimedia presentations and written reports.
Experience in coordination and collaboration with industry counterparts on technical projects, software and service assessment, and other related subject material.

Preferred Qualification

Experience with Intelligence Community (IC) and DoD geospatial data and repositories.
Experience working within common project management frameworks.
Demonstrated knowledge and experience in cartography, GIS, spatial modeling.
Demonstrated experience using Python, R, SAS, Java or other coding languages to deliver custom solutions.
Familiarity with Army, DoD, or IC geospatial processes, policy, and programs.
Private sector (e.g., GISP, Esri Professional, etc.) or government (e.g., GPC series) professional GIS certification.
Knowledge of Microsoft office tools and graphic design principles.
Familiarity with DoD/NSG Structured Observation Management (SOM) and object- based production

Location
Fort Gordon, GA

Physical Requirement

Work may involve sitting or standing for extended periods of time. Position may require typing and reading from a computer screen. to support the NOAA Office of Habitat Conservation’s NOAA Chesapeake Bay Office (NCBO) in Annapolis, MD. Data collection, standardization and processing: provide ingest, standardization, and processing for CBIBS, hypoxia, and other observational data to ensure quality and readiness for product integration.
Data Product Development: develop data and information products utilizing CBIBS, hypoxia and other observational data in support of NCBOs habitat and fisheries constituents.
Data visualization and interpretation: design intuitive visualizations and interpretive materials to effectively communicate data product insights to NCBO's habitat and fisheries constituents.

Telework is permitted, however, duties required such as vessel maintenance, equipment maintenance, and field work will require weekly presence at the Annapolis, MD office.

The salary for this position is approximately $60,000 - 70,000/year.

Demonstrated written and oral communication skills.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with peers, supervisors, agency officials and others.

Demonstrated operational knowledge of R-Studio or Python coding

Confirm project scope, expectations, timelines, and special requirements before work begins.
Identify missing information and proactively work with Sales, Operations, customers, and other stakeholders to resolve outstanding items.
Maintain a standardized project handoff process to ensure critical information does not fall through the cracks.
Document project conditions, specifications, photos, special instructions, and other information needed by the field team.

Maintain and update project schedules based on customer expectations, manpower availability, and operational capacity.

Help create a professional and organized customer experience from project award through field mobilization.

Assist with change documentation and other project-related administrative requirements as needed.

Help improve internal processes between Sales and Operations.
Support multiple active projects while maintaining accuracy, organization, and responsiveness.

Customer-service mindset with the ability to communicate professionally with customers and internal teams.

The Public Health Institute (PHI) is an independent, nonprofit organization dedicated to promoting health, well-being, and quality of life for people throughout California, across the nation and around the world. PHI was distinguished as one of the top 50 “Best Non-Profit Organizations to Work For” by the Non-Profit Times in a national search.

Position Summary

The original FACES for the Future Health Scholars program was established in 2000 at Children’s Hospital of Oakland; in 2011 FACES programs moved under the fiscal sponsorship of Public Health Institute, which allowed the creation of FACES for the Future Coalition (www.facesforthefuture.org). The Coalition, now national, both runs its own programs in California and New Mexico and supports affiliate members in San Diego and Colorado. Innovative and health careers focused, there are three main FACES programs: Health Scholars, Public Health Youth Corps, and the Summer Medical Academy. All FACES programs serve public high school students interested in public, medical, behavioral and global health careers. The Coalition’s work also includes new program and curriculum development, technical assistance consulting, evaluation, marketing and communications, and fund development.

The FACES for the Future Coalition is looking for a Program Coordinator for the FACES program in Albuquerque, New Mexico. The FACES program will be working with students and teachers to create work-based learning experiences to build capacity at partner school sites. This person will be primarily responsible for the planning, coordination, and supervision of daily operations. This includes host advisory committee meetings, implementation and supervision of clinical internship placements and rotations, academic support and mentoring, and coordination of the wellness program for students. The Program Coordinator is responsible for ensuring that all students meet the program expectations regarding training, performance, rules and behavior. new_jobs.description:
The Public Health Institute (PHI) is an independent, nonprofit organization dedicated to promoting health, well-being, and quality of life for people throughout California, across the nation and around the world. As one of the largest and most comprehensive public health organizations in the nation, we are at the forefront of research and innovations to improve the efficacy of public health statewide, nationally, and internationally.

PHI was distinguished as one of the top 50 “Best Non-Profit Organizations to Work For” by the Non-Profit Times in a national search.

Position Summary

The original FACES for the Future Health Scholars program was established in 2000 at Children’s Hospital of Oakland; in 2011 FACES programs moved under the fiscal sponsorship of Public Health Institute, which allowed the creation of FACES for the Future Coalition (www.facesforthefuture.org). The Coalition, now national, both runs its own programs in California and New Mexico and supports affiliate members in San Diego and Colorado. Innovative and health careers focused, there are three main FACES programs: Health Scholars, Public Health Youth Corps, and the Summer Medical Academy. All FACES programs serve public high school students interested in public, medical, behavioral and global health careers. The Coalition’s work also includes new program and curriculum development, technical assistance consulting, evaluation, marketing and communications, and fund development.

The FACES for the Future Coalition is looking for a Program Coordinator for the FACES program in Albuquerque, New Mexico. The FACES program will be working with students and teachers to create work-based learning experiences to build capacity at partner school sites. This person will be primarily responsible for the planning, coordination, and supervision of daily operations. This includes host advisory committee meetings, implementation and supervision of clinical internship placements and rotations, academic support and mentoring, and coordination of the wellness program for students. The Program Coordinator is responsible for ensuring that all students meet the program expectations regarding training, performance, rules and behavior. The Program Coordinator will work to guarantee that program materials are current and relevant, that operations run in a smooth and effective manner, and that open and regular communication exists with all program partners and stakeholders including health care professionals, health agency administration, school administration, teachers, students and families.

This is a time-limited, part-time (50% FTE) position that is expected to have a work schedule of 20 hours/week and end on May 28, 2027, with a possibility to extend based on funding availability.

This hybrid position is required to work remotely in the region of Albuquerque, NM and in person at school sites in Albuquerque, NM where student activities take place. The incumbent must have access to reliable transportation and ability to commute to various locations within a workday for community outreach, FACES events, and health pathways including, but not limited to, health fairs, recruitment events, and community showcases, and attending meetings with health employer partners as required.

Full salary range for this position: $65,962 to $94,454 per year at 100% FTE. The typical hiring range for this position is from $32,981 (minimum) to $40,104 (midpoint), based on 50% FTE. The starting salary is determined using a variety of factors, such as the candidate’s knowledge, skills, and experience, as well as internal equity consideration and budget availability.

Employment Type: Part Time

Schedule, facilitate, and teach workshops and trainings for students focused on health professions, college preparation, professional skills, wellness, and other assigned topics
Coordinate FACES events including Blue Coat Ceremony, graduations, field trips, and other special events
Recruit students, provide training to prepare students and preceptors for internships
Coordinate all necessary steps to on-board students into work-based learning including health screening requirements and communication with parents/guardians

Maintain adequate, organized documentation including databases and all program materials including, but not limited to, student information and records, curriculum, workshops attendance, evaluations, and program expenses

Provide regular written program updates to a multitude of stakeholders, including health employers, academic partners, and families as appropriate

Participate in relevant school and community health events to promote student accomplishments, FACES programming, and recruit potential health professionals

Coordinate advisory committee stakeholder meetings and recruit members as applicable
